title: Lang theorem for torsors under connected groups over finite fields
statement: Let $k$ be a finite field [def-weil-field], and let $H$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Y$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a right action $Y\times_kH\to Y$ satisfying the unit and associativity identities. Suppose that $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat and surjective and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and that $(y,h)\mapsto(y,yh)$ is an isomorphism $Y\times_kH\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_kY$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $Y(k)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}k,Y)$ is nonempty. Reductivity, commutativity and a chosen point of $Y$ are not hypotheses.

source.place: Corollary 17.98 and its proof, printed p.383; Proposition 3.50, p.80 (smooth-group torsors and H^1), Definition 2.66 and Proposition 2.69, p.60. This is the torsor form used in the proof of Theorem 25.9(b), p.546.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism and $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the induced morphism, and put $Y_K=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ with projections $p:Y_K\to Y$ and $f_K:Y_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. By [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] with $C=Y$, $f_K(Y_K)=g^{-1}(f(Y))$; since $f$ is surjective this is all of $\operatorname{Spec}K$, so $Y_K$ is nonempty. The only nonempty affine open of the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is itself, so the affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] cover $Y$ with each $A$ a finitely presented, in particular finitely generated, $k$-algebra: $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], $f_K$ is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] to the nonempty closed subset $Y_K$ itself to obtain a closed point. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] its residue field is $K$. The corresponding $K$-point, composed with $p$, gives $y\in Y(K)$.

source.place: Corollary 17.98 and proof, printed p.383; Proposition 3.50, p.80, and Definition 2.66, p.60: point representative of a torsor cocycle.

proof.text: Put $q=|k|$ [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements] and $\sigma(b)=b^q$ on $K$ [def-weil-frobenius-substitution]. For any $k$-scheme $T$ define $\sigma(t)=t\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ on $T(K)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Because the action is a $k$-morphism, $\sigma(yh)=\sigma(y)\sigma(h)$. Evaluate the assumed torsor isomorphism on $\operatorname{Spec}K$: the pair $(y,\sigma(y))$ has a unique preimage $(y,a)$, so $a\in H(K)$ and $\sigma(y)=ya$. This uses no prior $k$-point of $Y$.

source.place: Corollary 17.98 and proof, printed p.383; Proposition 3.50, p.80, and Definition 2.66, p.60: point representative of a torsor cocycle.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-lang-finite-field-group-surjectivity] to $H$ and $a$. Its hypotheses hold: $k$ is finite, $K$ is its algebraic closure, and $H$ is affine, smooth and of finite type; geometric connectedness gives connectedness by taking the extension $k/k$. Its Frobenius action on points is exactly that of step 2, since on any coordinate $c$ precomposition sends $h(c)$ to $h(c)^q$. Obtain $g\in H(K)$ with $g^{-1}\sigma(g)=a$, equivalently $\sigma(g)=ga$. Set $z=yg^{-1}$. Then, using the right action and keeping the factor order, $\sigma(z)=ya(ga)^{-1}=yaa^{-1}g^{-1}=yg^{-1}=z$.

source.place: Corollary 17.98 and proof, printed p.383; Proposition 3.50, p.80, and Definition 2.66, p.60: point representative of a torsor cocycle.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Y$ containing the image of $z$. The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$ factors through this open; write its ring map as $v:A\to K$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Equality $\sigma(z)=z$ says $v(b)^q=v(b)$ for every $b\in A$. By [lem-weil-unique-subfield-of-closure], clause 3 with $n=1$, the elements of $K$ satisfying this equation are exactly the image $\iota(k)$. Corestrict $v$ to $\iota(k)$ and compose with $\iota^{-1}$ to obtain a $k$-algebra map $A\to k$: its addition, multiplication and unit identities follow from those of $v$ and injectivity of $\iota$. Taking spectra and composing with $U\hookrightarrow Y$ gives a $k$-point of $Y$. No global affine or separated hypothesis on $Y$ was used.
